Explain why mammals and birds need double circulation but fish do not.
questions.modelAnswer: Mammals and birds are warm-blooded: they keep a constant body temperature, which needs a lot of energy and so a lot of oxygen. Double circulation keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood completely separate and sends blood to the body at high pressure, giving an efficient oxygen supply. Fish are cold-blooded and need less energy, so single circulation through a two-chambered heart is enough.
rubric: Separation of oxygenated/deoxygenated blood, high pressure
